comparison: Perfect alignment on claims C1, C6-C8 regarding conventional cryo-EM limitations. Both evaluations accept these background claims about concentration requirements without challenge, supported by established literature.

Strong agreement on claims C2, C22-C29, C61-C67 demonstrating MagIC-cryo-EM effectiveness at ultra-low concentrations. OpenEval emphasizes quantitative metrics (3.6 Å resolution, 55.7% enrichment, 5 ng/grid), while peer reviewers praise it as 'an important new tool' with 'convincing atomic structures.' Both find the method well-validated.

Strong agreement on claims C4, C38-C41, C66 regarding DuSTER method. Both evaluations accept DuSTER as effective for filtering low-signal particles. OpenEval validates technical aspects (contrast analysis, defocus distribution), while peer reviewers acknowledge it 'increases true positive detections' for the challenging NPM2 complex.

Strong agreement on claims C3, C32-C35 regarding H1.8-bound nucleosome structural similarity across cell cycle stages. Both evaluations accept that positional preferences don't explain reduced H1.8 association. Peer Reviewer 1 directly affirms the authors' interpretation.

Agreement on claims C19-C21, C80 regarding spacer module design. Both evaluations praise the spacer solution. OpenEval documents technical validation, while peer reviewers call it 'clever design' that minimizes bead interference. OpenEval also covers C15-C18 (halo problem identification) which peer R8 addresses.

Agreement on claims C15-C18 regarding the halo artifact problem. OpenEval documents the technical problem and its discovery, while peer reviewers implicitly accept these observations as they form the rationale for the spacer design that all reviewers praise.

Agreement on claims C9-C14, C31 regarding prior work and biological context. Both evaluations accept this background without challenge. OpenEval notes appropriate citations, peer reviewers acknowledge the prior Arimura et al. work. Peer R11 also covers additional background claims C47-C50, C69-C70.

Partial overlap on NPM2 discovery pipeline. OpenEval R4 covers claims C36-C46 (fractionation, MS identification, structural matching), while peer R5 focuses on claims C5, C36, C42-C46, C68 (discovery and interphase enrichment). Both affirm the NPM2 discovery, with peer reviewers noting it provides 'mechanistic insights.'

Strong agreement on claims C51-C60 regarding NPM2 structural characterization (open/closed forms, H1.8 density, stoichiometry). OpenEval provides detailed structural validation, peer reviewers accept the structures as 'convincing' and note caveats were addressed in revision. Peer R6 also addresses mechanistic claims C73-C76.

Partial overlap on NPM2 mechanistic model. OpenEval R8 covers claims C73-C79 (pentameric state, substrate-induced transitions, flexibility), while peer R6 addresses C73-C76. Both evaluations accept the mechanistic interpretations, with peer reviewers noting structures provide 'mechanistic insights.'

Partial overlap on mechanistic interpretations. OpenEval R8 covers structural basis claims C73-C79, while peer R7 addresses functional interpretations C71-C72, C77-C79. Both accept the mechanistic framework, with peer reviewers noting 'caveats have been addressed' and conclusions are strengthened.

Agreement on claims C71-C72 regarding chromatin-specific mechanism for H1.8-NPM2 interaction. Both evaluations accept the mechanistic model integrating structural and biochemical findings. Peer reviewers affirm the interpretations provide insights into 'reduced affinity of H1.8 to interphase chromatin.'

Minimal overlap on claim C68 (NPM2-H1.8 complexes predominant in interphase). OpenEval R7 integrates this into mechanistic model with C68-C72, while peer R5 includes C68 in the discovery validation. Both accept the finding.

Agreement on claims C47-C50 regarding NPM2 background knowledge. Both evaluations accept this established literature without challenge. OpenEval notes appropriate citations, peer reviewers implicitly accept as necessary context. Peer R11 covers broader background including C9-C14, C30-C31, C69-C70.

Agreement on claim C81 regarding H1.8-GFP functionality. OpenEval notes this supports biological relevance of findings, peer reviewers implicitly accept the tagged construct as valid, noting GFP-tagged structures are 'essentially identical' to endogenous.

Partial overlap on claims C38-C42 regarding DuSTER development and NPM2 discovery. OpenEval R4 emphasizes the discovery pipeline convergence, while peer R3 focuses on DuSTER's effectiveness. Both accept the methodological innovation and its role in enabling NPM2 identification.

Minimal overlap on claim C5 (NPM2 structural characterization). OpenEval R6 provides detailed structural analysis C5, C51-C60, while peer R5 includes C5 in broader discovery validation. Both accept the structural findings as convincing.

Minimal overlap on claims C69-C70 (consistency with literature, cytoplasmic NPM2 levels). OpenEval R7 uses these to support chromatin-specific mechanism inference, while peer R11 accepts as background context. Both evaluations support these claims.

Minimal overlap on claim C30 (prior work context). OpenEval R3 includes C30 in H1.8 structural analysis context, while peer R11 accepts as background. Both evaluations accept this prior work without challenge.
